'''Andrew Bruce Bocarsly''' (born April 23, 1954) is currently a professor at [[Princeton University]], [[New Jersey]]. His primary [[research]] interests lie in physical inorganic chemistry.<ref>{{cite book |last1=American Chemical Society. Committee on Professional Training |title=Directory of Graduate Research |date=2005 |publisher=American Chemical Society |location=Washington|pages=799–800}}</ref> He conducts research in [[electrochemistry]], photochemistry, solids state chemistry, and fuel cells, and is known for his work on alternate energy solutions involving processes and materials for photo-reduction and electro-reduction.<ref name="Khan">{{cite web |last1=Khan |first1=Fahd S. |title=Princeton University's Visiting Student Research Collaborator (VSRC) program |url=https://www.friendsofutokyo.org/princeton-universitys-visiting-student-research-collaborator-vsrc-program/ |website=Friends of UTokyo |date=20 April 2016 |accessdate=21 May 2019}}</ref><ref name="CV">{{cite web|url=http://chemlabs.princeton.edu/bocarsly/wp-content/uploads/sites/26/2016/10/ABB-short-cv-2016.pdf |title=Andrew B. Bocarsly Professor of Chemistry |website=Princeton University }}</ref><ref name="Kincade">{{cite news |last1=Kincade |first1=Kathy |title=Turning Greenhouse Gases into Gold NERSC simulations reveal reaction mechanism behind CO2 conversion into carbon-neutral fuels and chemicals |url=https://cs.lbl.gov/news-media/news/2013/turning-greenhouse-gases-into-gold/ |accessdate=21 May 2019 |work=Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory |date=November 6, 2013}}</ref>

==Education and career ==
Bocarsly graduated with a B.S., magna cum laude, from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] with a double major in chemistry and physics (June 1976). There he worked with John Gladysz on [[research]] involving [[metal vapor synthesis]]. In June 1980 he received his PhD from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] for research on charge transfer processes on [[semiconductors]]. Starting in 1980, he was assistant and associate professor at [[Princeton University]] where he is currently a full [[professor]]. Bocarsly currently teaches the second course of the introductory General Chem sequence at Princeton. <ref name="ICCDU">{{cite web |title=Plenary speakers |url=http://iccdu2016.org.uk/the-conference/plenary-speakers |website=International Conference on Carbon Dioxide Utilisation 2016 |accessdate=21 May 2019}}</ref>

==Carbon dioxide==

Bocarsly's publications include around 200 refereed journal papers,<ref name="White"/> multiple patents,<ref>{{cite web |title=Patents by Inventor Andrew B. Bocarsly |url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/andrew-b-bocarsly |website=Justia |accessdate=22 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Patents by Inventor Andrew Bocarsly |url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/andrew-bocarsly |website=Justia |accessdate=22 May 2019}}</ref> and the edited book ''Fuel Cells and Hydrogen Storage'' (2011).<ref name="Mingos">{{cite book |editor-last1=Bocarsly |editor-first1=Andrew |editor-last2=Mingos |editor-first2=David Michael P. |title='Fuel Cells and Hydrogen Storage |date=July 29, 2011 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media}}</ref>
Bocarsly has published on catalysts for the reduction of [[carbon dioxide]] to organic products.<ref name="Parker">{{cite news |last1=Parker |first1=Hilary |title=Celebrate Princeton Invention: Andrew Bocarsly |url=http://www.princeton.edu/main/news/archive/S26/14/19A34/index.xml |accessdate=21 May 2019 |work=Princeton News |date=December 21, 2009}}</ref><ref name="Yan">{{cite journal |last1=Yan |first1=Yong |last2=Zeitler |first2=Elizabeth L. |last3=Gu |first3=Jing |last4=Hu |first4=Yuan |last5=Bocarsly |first5=Andrew B. |title=Electrochemistry of Aqueous Pyridinium: Exploration of a Key Aspect of Electrocatalytic Reduction of CO to Methanol |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |date=17 September 2013 |volume=135 |issue=38 |pages=14020–14023 |doi=10.1021/ja4064052 |pmid=23972003 |bibcode=2013JAChS.13514020Y }}</ref><ref name="Paris">{{cite journal |last1=Paris |first1=Aubrey R. |last2=Chu |first2=An T. |last3=B. O'Brien |first3=Conor |last4=Frick |first4=Jessica J. |last5=Francis |first5=Sonja A. |last6=Bocarsly |first6=Andrew B. |title=Tuning the Products of CO Electroreduction on a Ni Ga Catalyst Using Carbon Solid Supports |journal=Journal of the Electrochemical Society |date=15 May 2018 |volume=165 |issue=7 |pages=H385–H392 |doi=10.1149/2.0791807jes |s2cid=104835529 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
With [[Emily Barton Cole]], he has worked on the selective conversion of carbon dioxide to methanol.<ref name="Biello">{{cite news |last1=Biello |first1=David |title=Reverse Combustion: Can CO2 Be Turned Back into Fuel? |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/turning-carbon-dioxide-back-into-fuel/ |accessdate=21 May 2019 |work=Scientific American |date=September 23, 2010}}</ref><ref name="WVCA2015">{{cite news |title=New Jersey and Virginia Convert CO2 into Ethanol for US Gov |url=https://www.wvcoal.com/research-development/new-jersey-and-virginia-convert-co2-into-ethanol-for-us-gov |accessdate=21 May 2019 |work=West Virginia Coal Association |date=August 3, 2015}}</ref> 
<ref name="Barton">{{cite journal |last1=Barton |first1=Emily E. |last2=Rampulla |first2=David M. |last3=Bocarsly |first3=Andrew B. |title=Selective Solar-Driven Reduction of CO to Methanol Using a Catalyzed p-GaP Based Photoelectrochemical Cell |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |date=May 2008 |volume=130 |issue=20 |pages=6342–6344 |doi=10.1021/ja0776327 |pmid=18439010|bibcode=2008JAChS.130.6342B }}</ref><ref name="Barton Cole">{{cite journal |last1=Barton Cole |first1=Emily |last2=Lakkaraju |first2=Prasad S. |last3=Rampulla |first3=David M. |last4=Morris |first4=Amanda J. |last5=Abelev |first5=Esta |last6=Bocarsly |first6=Andrew B. |title=Using a One-Electron Shuttle for the Multielectron Reduction of CO to Methanol: Kinetic, Mechanistic, and Structural Insights |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |date=25 August 2010 |volume=132 |issue=33 |pages=11539–11551 |doi=10.1021/ja1023496 |pmid=20666494|bibcode=2010JAChS.13211539B }}</ref>
This interest in [[artificial photosynthesis]] led to the founding of the company [[Liquid Light]] in 2009.<ref name="Biello"/><ref name="Alperin">{{cite news |last1=Alperin |first1=Michele |title=Liquid Light Wastes Not, but Hopes for a Lot |url=https://princetoninfo.com/liquid-light-wastes-not-but-hopes-for-a-lot/ |accessdate=21 May 2019 |work=Princeton Info |date=July 28, 2010}}</ref><ref name="Dunn">{{cite news |last1=Dunn |first1=Laura Emily |title=Women in Business Q&A: Dr. Emily Cole, Co-Founder, Liquid Light |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/women-in-business-qa-dr-e_b_6782978 |accessdate=21 May 2019 |work=HuffPost |date=March 2, 2015}}</ref><ref name="Rogers">{{cite news |last1=Levine |first1=Barry |last2=Rogers |first2=Stewart |title=Find out who made VentureBeat's first 'Naughty & Nice' list |url=https://venturebeat.com/business/find-out-who-made-venturebeats-first-naughty-nice-list |access-date=21 May 2019 |work=VentureBeat |date=December 23, 2014}}</ref><ref name="Levine">{{cite news |last1=Levine |first1=Barry |title=Princeton researchers use sunlight to convert CO2 more efficiently than plants do |url=https://venturebeat.com/business/princeton-researchers-use-sunlight-to-convert-co2-more-efficiently-than-plants-do |access-date=22 May 2019 |work=Venture Beat |date=July 3, 2014}}</ref>
